stem_book: Prove that the equation p cos x − q sin x = r admits solution for x only if −√(p² + q²) < r < √(p² + q²).
reason: 'Prove that' question — subjective; also the printed strict inequalities should be ≤ (r = ±√(p²+q²) does give solutions).
work: p cos x − q sin x = √(p²+q²) cos(x + φ) ∈ [−√(p²+q²), √(p²+q²)]
